title: Analysis of the Derivatives of Sialic Acid in Pig Tissues
author: Chon-Ho Yen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zd6f29e
materials: HPLC system, Thermo Scientific™ (Waters 2475 Multi-wavelength Fluorescence Detector, Waters 717 plus Autosampler and Waters 600 Controller)

steps.title: Gather equipment and consumables
steps.instruction: Collect the following: Discovery® BIO wide‑pore C18 column (5 µm, 4.6 × 25 cm), Dry Bath Incubator (Violet BioScience Model VH01), centrifuge (Sigma 3K30), 0.22 µm membrane filters, methanol, acetonitrile, deionized water, 99.8 % acetic acid, 2‑mercaptoethanol, sodium hydrosulfite, DMB (Sigma‑Aldrich), 0.5 M H₂SO₄, and standard compounds NANA and NGNA.

steps.title: Prepare reagent buffer
steps.instruction: In a tube add 800 µL of 99.8 % acetic acid, 540 µL of 2‑mercaptoethanol, and 31 mg sodium hydrosulfite dissolved in 7 mL deionized water; then add deionized water to a final volume of 10 mL (final concentrations: 1.4 M acetic acid, 0.75 M 2‑ME, 18 mM sodium hydrosulfite).

steps.title: Prepare DMB labeling reagent
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.6 mg of DMB in 1 mL of the reagent buffer prepared above.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC mobile phase
steps.instruction: Into a 1 L volumetric flask add 70 mL methanol and 90 mL acetonitrile, then add deionized water to the mark (1000 mL total). Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm membrane.

steps.title: Process tissue samples
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 100 mg of pig tissue (ear, tail, or small intestine), place in deionized water, and cut into small pieces with scissors.

steps.title: Hydrolyze sialic acids
steps.instruction: Incubate the tissue mixture at 95 °C for 30 min. Cool to room temperature, add 0.5 M H₂SO₄ to reach a final concentration of 25 mM, then incubate at 80 °C for 1 h to release sialic acids.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the hydrolysate at 10 000 × g for 10 min and transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Prepare NANA and NGNA standards
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg of NANA in 1 mL deionized water and separately dissolve 1 mg of NGNA in 1 mL deionized water.

steps.title: Label samples and standards with DMB
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of DMB reagent to 200 µL of each sample supernatant or standard solution, mix, and incubate at 80 °C for 2 h to attach the fluorescent label.

steps.title: Filter labeled mixtures
steps.instruction: Pass each DMB‑labeled mixture through a 0.22 µm membrane filter.

steps.title: Dilute for HPLC analysis
steps.instruction: Dilute filtered samples 100‑fold with deionized water; dilute standards 5 000‑10 000‑fold with deionized water.

steps.title: Set up HPLC system and column
steps.instruction: Install the Discovery® BIO wide‑pore C18 column (5 µm, 4.6 × 25 cm) on the Waters™ HPLC system (2475 Fluorescence Detector, 717 Autosampler, 600 Controller).

steps.title: Configure HPLC run parameters
steps.instruction: Use an isocratic mobile phase of methanol : acetonitrile : water = 7 : 9 : 84, flow rate 0.6 mL/min, fluorescence detector set to excitation 373 nm and emission 448 nm.

steps.title: Inject samples and acquire data
steps.instruction: Inject the diluted, filtered, DMB‑labeled samples and standards onto the column and record fluorescence chromatograms under the configured conditions.
